display.title: Honoring Sifrei Kodesh: The Chumash, Hashem's Own Words
display.summary_short: A Mitzvah Time lesson: the Chumash is unlike any other book because its words come from Hashem, so we keep it clean and wash our hands before opening it.
display.summary_long: A short Mitzvah Time lesson from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, part of a series on kibbud sifrei kodesh, honoring holy books. Uncle Yossi reviews why the Chumash is different from every other book in the world: other books were written by people, but the Chumash holds the words of the Torah that Hashem Himself gave us, so reading it means reading Hashem's own words. Honoring the Chumash is honoring Hashem, the Giver of the Torah. He then reviews last week's rules: keep the Chumash, the Siddur and every holy book in good shape, clean and spotless, and wash your hands well before opening one, because clean fingers and clean hands mean a clean sefer.
display.lesson: The Chumash contains Hashem's own words, so treat it with honor and keep it clean.
